# verda object-storage (beta)

> Verda CLI **v1.10.0** · [other versions](https://github.com/verda-cloud/verda-cli/tags)

Manage S3 object storage

Manage S3-compatible object storage credentials and operations.

S3 credentials are stored separately from API credentials in the
same credentials file (~/.verda/credentials) using verda_s3_ prefixed keys.

Configure credentials:

```text
verda object-storage configure
```

Show current S3 credential status:

```text
verda object-storage show
```

Aliases: `oss`, `d4`

Subcommands:

- [`verda object-storage abort-uploads`](#verda-object-storage-abort-uploads): Abort in-progress multipart uploads to reclaim storage
- [`verda object-storage configure`](#verda-object-storage-configure): Configure S3 object storage credentials
- [`verda object-storage cp`](#verda-object-storage-cp): Copy files between local and S3, or between S3 buckets
- [`verda object-storage ls`](#verda-object-storage-ls): List buckets or objects in an S3 bucket
- [`verda object-storage ls-uploads`](#verda-object-storage-ls-uploads): List in-progress (incomplete) multipart uploads
- [`verda object-storage mb`](#verda-object-storage-mb): Create (make) an S3 bucket
- [`verda object-storage mv`](#verda-object-storage-mv): Move files between local and S3, or between S3 buckets
- [`verda object-storage presign`](#verda-object-storage-presign): Generate a presigned GET URL for an S3 object
- [`verda object-storage rb`](#verda-object-storage-rb): Remove (delete) an S3 bucket
- [`verda object-storage rm`](#verda-object-storage-rm): Delete objects from an S3 bucket
- [`verda object-storage show`](#verda-object-storage-show): Show S3 credential status
- [`verda object-storage sync`](#verda-object-storage-sync): Incrementally sync a directory/prefix with S3

## verda object-storage abort-uploads

Abort in-progress multipart uploads to reclaim storage

Abort in-progress (incomplete) multipart uploads in a bucket. The
staged parts of an incomplete upload consume real, billed storage
even though the object never appears in "verda object-storage ls". Aborting
reclaims that storage.

Use --older-than to abort only uploads initiated before a given age
(e.g. 7d, 12h), and --key to target a single object key. Without
either, EVERY in-progress upload in the bucket is aborted.

This is destructive: aborted uploads cannot be resumed and their
parts are deleted. In --agent mode, --yes is required.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage abort-uploads s3://bucket [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --key string          Only abort uploads for this exact object key
      --older-than string   Only abort uploads initiated before this age (e.g. 7d, 12h)
      --prefix string       Only abort uploads whose key starts with this prefix
      --yes                 Skip confirmation prompt
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Abort uploads older than 7 days
verda object-storage abort-uploads s3://my-bucket --older-than 7d

# Abort every in-progress upload (with confirmation)
verda object-storage abort-uploads s3://my-bucket

# Abort uploads for a single key
verda object-storage abort-uploads s3://my-bucket --key path/to/big.bin

# Skip the confirmation prompt
verda object-storage abort-uploads s3://my-bucket --older-than 30d --yes
```

## verda object-storage configure

Configure S3 object storage credentials

Save S3 object storage credentials to the shared credentials file.

Create an access key first in the Verda dashboard: log in, select your
project, then open Project management → Credentials → Object Storage
Access Keys. The endpoint and region are pre-filled with sensible
defaults, so you usually only need to paste the access key and secret.

S3 credentials are stored alongside API credentials using verda_s3_
prefixed keys. Profile switching (--profile) works across both.

Default file: ~/.verda/credentials
Override with --credentials-file or VERDA_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE.

Resolution order for every object-storage command, per field:

```text
1. Command flags (--access-key, --secret-key, --endpoint, --region)
2. VERDA_S3_ACCESS_KEY, VERDA_S3_SECRET_KEY, VERDA_S3_ENDPOINT,
   VERDA_S3_REGION, VERDA_S3_AUTH_MODE
3. The credentials-file profile above
```

The merge is per field, not all-or-nothing: setting only
VERDA_S3_ENDPOINT overrides the endpoint and keeps the profile's keys.
An empty variable counts as unset. A complete env set needs no file at
all, which is how CI avoids writing secrets to disk.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage configure [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --access-key string         S3 access key ID
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared credentials file
      --endpoint string           S3 endpoint URL
      --profile string            Credentials profile name (default "default")
      --region string             S3 region (default "eu-north-3")
      --secret-key string         S3 secret access key
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive wizard (prompts for all fields)
verda object-storage configure

# Non-interactive with flags
verda object-storage configure \
--access-key AKIA1234567890EXAMPLE \
--secret-key wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLE \
--endpoint https://objects.lab.verda.storage

# Different profile
verda object-storage configure \
--profile staging \
--access-key AKIA... \
--secret-key ... \
--endpoint https://staging.objects.verda.storage
```

## verda object-storage cp

Copy files between local and S3, or between S3 buckets

Copy files between local paths and S3 URIs, or between two S3
URIs. At least one of &lt;src&gt; or &lt;dst&gt; must be an s3:// URI.

With --recursive, uploads walk the local directory, and S3
downloads / copies paginate through every object under the
source prefix. --include and --exclude glob patterns filter
the set (matched against the relative path; '\*' does not
cross '/').

Large single-file uploads and single-object downloads are multipart

```text
and parallel, and they RESUME: re-run the EXACT same command to
continue an interrupted transfer (only the missing parts move).
--no-resume starts over; --concurrency / --part-size tune throughput.
Interactive downloads from the "verda object-storage ls" browser resume the same way.

With --dryrun, the planned transfers are listed but no SDK
```

calls are made.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage cp <src> <dst> [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --concurrency int       Parallel parts for large uploads/downloads (default 5)
      --content-type string   Override Content-Type on uploads
      --dryrun                Preview transfers without performing them
      --exclude stringArray   Skip entries matching this glob (repeatable, overrides --include)
      --include stringArray   Only copy entries matching this glob (repeatable)
      --no-resume             Ignore saved progress and restart the transfer (upload or download)
      --part-size string      Part size for large uploads/downloads, e.g. 32MiB (default auto)
      --recursive             Copy every file under a directory/prefix
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Upload a single file
verda object-storage cp ./report.csv s3://my-bucket/reports/report.csv

# Upload into a "folder" (trailing slash keeps the filename)
verda object-storage cp ./report.csv s3://my-bucket/reports/

# Download a single object
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/report.csv ./report.csv

# Download into a directory (keeps the object's name)
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/report.csv ./downloads/

# Recursively download a whole prefix
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/logs/ ./logs --recursive

# Resume an interrupted upload or download — re-run the same command
verda object-storage cp ./model.bin s3://my-bucket/model.bin
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/model.bin ./model.bin

# Faster large transfer
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/model.bin ./model.bin --concurrency 16 --part-size 32MiB

# Copy between buckets
verda object-storage cp s3://src/a.txt s3://dst/b.txt

# Recursive upload with filter
verda object-storage cp ./data s3://my-bucket/data/ --recursive --include "*.csv"

# Recursive upload, skipping temp files
verda object-storage cp ./site s3://my-bucket/site/ --recursive --exclude "*.tmp"

# Override the content type on upload
verda object-storage cp ./page.html s3://my-bucket/page.html --content-type text/html

# Preview a recursive download
verda object-storage cp s3://my-bucket/logs/ ./logs --recursive --dryrun
```

## verda object-storage ls

List buckets or objects in an S3 bucket

List buckets when invoked with no arguments, or list the
top-level keys + common prefixes under an s3:// URI.

Pass --recursive to flatten all keys under the prefix.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage ls [s3://bucket[/prefix/]] [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --human-readable   Display sizes in human-friendly units (KB, MB, ...)
      --recursive        List all keys under the prefix (no delimiter)
      --summarize        Append a total objects/size footer
```

**Examples**

```bash
# List all buckets
verda object-storage ls

# List top-level keys under a bucket
verda object-storage ls s3://my-bucket

# List keys under a prefix
verda object-storage ls s3://my-bucket/prefix/

# Recursively list every key in the bucket
verda object-storage ls s3://my-bucket --recursive

# Human-readable sizes + summary
verda object-storage ls s3://my-bucket --human-readable --summarize
```

## verda object-storage ls-uploads

List in-progress (incomplete) multipart uploads

List in-progress multipart uploads in a bucket. The staged parts of
an incomplete upload consume real storage and are billed even though
the object does not appear in "verda object-storage ls". This command surfaces
that hidden cost: key, UploadId, when it was initiated, and the
accumulated size of the parts uploaded so far.

Use "verda object-storage abort-uploads" to reclaim the storage.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage ls-uploads s3://bucket [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --prefix string   Only list uploads whose key starts with this prefix
```

**Examples**

```bash
# List every in-progress upload in a bucket
verda object-storage ls-uploads s3://my-bucket

# Only uploads under a key prefix
verda object-storage ls-uploads s3://my-bucket --prefix logs/

# Machine-readable output
verda object-storage ls-uploads s3://my-bucket -o json
```

## verda object-storage mb

Create (make) an S3 bucket

Create a new S3 bucket. The URI must be a bucket-only URI
(s3://bucket) with no key component.

Run with no argument on a terminal to be prompted for the name.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage mb s3://bucket [flags]
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Create a new bucket
verda object-storage mb s3://my-new-bucket

# Prompt for the name interactively
verda object-storage mb
```

## verda object-storage mv

Move files between local and S3, or between S3 buckets

Move files between local paths and S3 URIs, or between two S3
URIs. At least one of &lt;src&gt; or &lt;dst&gt; must be an s3:// URI. A
move is a copy followed by a delete of the source — the source
is only removed once the transfer succeeds.

With --recursive, local moves walk the directory and S3 moves
paginate through every object under the source prefix.
--include and --exclude glob patterns filter the set (matched
against the relative path; '\*' does not cross '/').

With --dryrun, the planned moves are listed but no SDK calls
or local filesystem changes are made.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage mv <src> <dst> [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --content-type string   Override Content-Type on uploads
      --dryrun                Preview moves without performing them
      --exclude stringArray   Skip entries matching this glob (repeatable, overrides --include)
      --include stringArray   Only move entries matching this glob (repeatable)
      --recursive             Move every file under a directory/prefix
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Move a single file to S3 (removes the local source on success)
verda object-storage mv ./report.csv s3://my-bucket/reports/report.csv

# Move an object out of S3 to local disk
verda object-storage mv s3://my-bucket/report.csv ./report.csv

# Move between buckets
verda object-storage mv s3://src/a.txt s3://dst/b.txt

# Recursive move of every .csv file under a directory
verda object-storage mv ./data s3://my-bucket/data/ --recursive --include "*.csv"

# Preview a recursive move
verda object-storage mv s3://my-bucket/logs/ ./logs --recursive --dryrun

# Move/rename an object interactively (S3 -> S3)
verda object-storage mv
```

## verda object-storage presign

Generate a presigned GET URL for an S3 object

Generate a time-limited HTTPS URL that grants GET access to an
object without exposing your S3 credentials. The URL expires after
the duration given by --expires-in (default 1h).

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage presign s3://bucket/key [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --expires-in duration   URL expiration (e.g. 15m, 1h, 24h) (default 1h0m0s)
```

**Examples**

```bash
verda object-storage presign s3://my-bucket/report.csv
verda object-storage presign s3://my-bucket/report.csv --expires-in 15m
verda object-storage presign s3://my-bucket/report.csv --expires-in 24h
```

## verda object-storage rb

Remove (delete) an S3 bucket

Remove an S3 bucket. The bucket must be empty unless --force is
passed, in which case all objects are deleted first in batches.

This action is destructive and cannot be undone. In --agent mode,
--yes is required to proceed.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage rb s3://bucket [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --force   Empty the bucket before deletion
      --yes     Skip confirmation prompt
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Remove an empty bucket
verda object-storage rb s3://my-bucket

# Remove a non-empty bucket (deletes all objects first)
verda object-storage rb s3://my-bucket --force

# Skip confirmation prompt
verda object-storage rb s3://my-bucket --yes
```

## verda object-storage rm

Delete objects from an S3 bucket

Delete one or more objects from an S3 bucket.

Without --recursive the URI must specify a single object key;
with --recursive the URI is treated as a prefix and every
matching object under it is deleted. --include and --exclude
glob patterns filter the recursive set (matched against the
full key; '\*' does not cross '/'). Excludes take precedence
over includes.

Pass --dryrun to preview the set of keys without issuing any
deletes. In --agent mode, --yes is required unless --dryrun
is also passed.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage rm s3://bucket/key [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --dryrun                Preview deletions without performing them
      --exclude stringArray   Skip keys matching this glob (repeatable, overrides --include)
      --include stringArray   Only delete keys matching this glob (repeatable)
      --recursive             Treat the URI as a prefix and delete all matching objects
      --yes                   Skip confirmation prompt
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Delete a single object
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/path/to/obj.txt

# Recursively delete every object under a prefix
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/logs/ --recursive

# Only delete .txt files, keep everything else
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/data/ --recursive --include "*.txt"

# Delete everything except .log files
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/data/ --recursive --exclude "*.log"

# Preview without deleting
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/data/ --recursive --dryrun

# Skip confirmation
verda object-storage rm s3://my-bucket/obj --yes

# Browse and tick files to delete interactively
verda object-storage rm
```

## verda object-storage show

Show S3 credential status

Show the current S3 credentials status for a profile.
Secret values are not displayed — only whether they are loaded.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage show [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared credentials file
      --profile string            Credentials profile to show (default: active profile)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Show default profile
verda object-storage show

# Show specific profile
verda object-storage show --profile staging
```

## verda object-storage sync

Incrementally sync a directory/prefix with S3

Recursively sync files between a local directory and an S3
prefix, between two S3 prefixes, or in either direction. Only
new or updated files are copied; unchanged files are skipped.

By default a file is considered "updated" when the source is
newer OR the sizes differ. Pass --exact-timestamps to require
the timestamps match exactly (any difference triggers a copy).

With --delete, files present at the destination but not at the
source are removed after the copy phase. Include/exclude glob
filters are applied to the relative path on BOTH sides — an
excluded key is neither copied nor deleted.

With --dryrun, the planned copies/deletes are listed but no SDK
calls or local filesystem changes are made.

**Usage**

```text
verda object-storage sync <src> <dst> [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --delete                Delete destination files that have no corresponding source
      --dryrun                Preview planned copies/deletes without performing them
      --exact-timestamps      Require exact timestamp match instead of src-newer
      --exclude stringArray   Skip entries matching this glob (repeatable, overrides --include)
      --include stringArray   Only sync entries matching this glob (repeatable)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Mirror a local directory to S3
verda object-storage sync ./site s3://my-bucket/site/

# Pull a prefix down incrementally
verda object-storage sync s3://my-bucket/backups/ ./backups

# Copy between buckets, mirroring deletions
verda object-storage sync s3://src/data/ s3://dst/data/ --delete

# Only sync .csv files, preview first
verda object-storage sync ./data s3://my-bucket/data/ --include "*.csv" --dryrun
```

---

Global flags such as `--output`, `--agent` and `--debug` work with every command: see [Global Flags](../commands.md#global-flags).
